$\cos\theta=0.6=\dfrac{3}{5}$, with $\cos\theta>0$ and $\sin\theta<0$, so $\theta$ is in Quadrant 4 and $\tan\theta<0$. Using the triangle with sides 3, 4, 5, $\tan\theta=-\dfrac{4}{3}$, so $\cot\theta=-\dfrac{3}{4}$.

solutions.latex:
At $x=-2$, $f'(x)=0$, so it is a stationary point. Also $f''(x)>0$ on the left of $x=-2$ and $f''(x)<0$ on the right, so there is a change in concavity, so a (horizontal) point of inflexion.

Alternatively, $f'(x)$ is 0 at $x=-2$ but negative on both sides of $-2$, so an inflexion.

$y=x\sin x$, so $y'=\sin x\cdot1+x\cos x$.

At $x=\dfrac\pi2$, $y=\dfrac\pi2\sin\dfrac\pi2=\dfrac\pi2$ and $y'=\sin\dfrac\pi2+\dfrac\pi2\cos\dfrac\pi2=1$, so $m_N=-1$.

solutions.latex: If $|x|-2x=3$ then $|x|=2x+3$, so $|x|-1=2x+2$. So the solution is where the graphs intersect in part (a), so $x=-1$.
$l=r\theta$, so $r+r+r\theta=8$, so $2r+r\theta=8$, so $r(2+\theta)=8$, so $r=\dfrac{8}{2+\theta}$ as required.

$$\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=\dfrac{(\theta+2)^2\cdot32-(32\theta)\cdot2(\theta+2)}{(\theta+2)^4}$$

For a maximum $\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=0$, so $32(\theta+2)^2-64\theta(\theta+2)=0$, so $32(\theta+2)[\theta+2-2\theta]=0$, so $32(\theta+2)(2-\theta)=0$, so $\theta=-2$ or $\theta=2$.

But $0\le\theta\le\dfrac\pi2$, so these both lie outside the possible range of $\theta$. So we test the endpoints $0$ and $\dfrac\pi2$:

At $\theta=0$, $A=0$.

At $\theta=\dfrac\pi2$, $A=\dfrac{32\left(\frac\pi2\right)}{\left(\frac\pi2+2\right)^2}=\dfrac{16\pi}{\left(\frac{\pi+4}{2}\right)^2}=\dfrac{64\pi}{(\pi+4)^2}\doteq3.9422\ \text{cm}^2$.

Thus the maximum area is $\dfrac{64\pi}{(\pi+4)^2}\ \text{cm}^2\doteq3.9422\ \text{cm}^2$, obtained when $\theta=\dfrac\pi2$ radians.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct maximum area and value of $\theta$; 1: correct derivative (ticks at derivative and final answer)

notes: Cover says 'Assessment Task 3' but the job metadata calls this the trial (AT4), so cover.task_code is AT4. Printed Q13 and Q14 each group two unrelated items under one lead-in; stored as 13(a), 13(b), 14(a), 14(b) (lead-in kept in each part, so it reads 'integrals'/'functions' in the plural for a single item). seq runs 1-40 for the 40 stored questions (38 printed numbers). Source file 1300 pages 51-65 (0-based) hold a separate set of 'Question 1 (7 Marks)' to 'Question 7' with a table of marking guidelines (pool draining, present value tables, particle with exponential velocity, AP loan repayments, toxic concentration, house loan, particle x = 1 - cos 2t). They do not belong to this paper (cover totals 100 marks for Q1-38, no school name on them, question numbers repeat 1-7) and were NOT parsed; a human should check where they came from. Solutions come from the handwritten worked solutions (scan, same content in bundled file 1300 pages 27-50 and file 1287); marks_breakdown is based on the tick marks on the scripts, since no written marking criteria are printed for Q1-38.
